author: L. G. Koenig
title: Sacred Heart women's basketball defeats Siena behind Amelia Wood's double-double
text:
Jessica Mannetti, Head Coach at Sacred Heart Pioneers Women's Basketball | https://sacredheartpioneers.com/
Jessica Mannetti, Head Coach at Sacred Heart Pioneers Women's Basketball | https://sacredheartpioneers.com/
The Sacred Heart University women's basketball team secured a 70-58 win over Siena on Wednesday, marking their fifth victory in Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference (MAAC) play this season. Senior Amelia Wood led the Pioneers with a double-double, scoring 21 points and collecting 12 rebounds. This performance marked her fourth double-double of the season and her fifth game reaching at least 20 points.
First-year player Sophie Nascimento contributed 17 points, with 15 coming in the first half, including an 11-point second quarter that helped build a 10-point halftime lead for Sacred Heart. Junior Nalyce Dudley added 12 points to the team's total.
Sacred Heart shot 51 percent from the field, making 25 of their 49 attempts. The team also hit six three-pointers and converted on 14 of their 21 free throw opportunities. After allowing Siena to shoot nearly 59 percent in the opening quarter, Sacred Heart's defense tightened, limiting Siena to just ten made shots out of their last forty-eight attempts over the final three quarters. In the second quarter alone, Siena went without a field goal.
Wood said she was pleased with both her own and her team's performance as they improved their conference record to five wins and two losses. The Pioneers now hold an overall record of seven wins and nine losses.
Sacred Heart started strong with early baskets from Emma Kirby and Wood but trailed by six after one quarter as Siena saw contributions from several players. The second quarter turned in Sacred Heart’s favor when Nascimento sparked a run that led to a significant halftime advantage.
In the third quarter, Sierra Johnson opened scoring for Sacred Heart with a three-pointer while Missy Nuku extended the lead to its largest margin at seventeen points midway through the period. Siena managed only brief runs but could not close the gap significantly.
Kirby again provided early offense in the fourth quarter for Sacred Heart before Siena attempted a comeback that was ultimately held off by strong Pioneer defense and solid free throw shooting down the stretch.
Looking ahead, Sacred Heart will travel to face Rider in southern New Jersey on Saturday, January 17. This will be their first repeat matchup against a MAAC opponent this season as part of eight scheduled home-and-home series within conference play. Tip-off is set for 2:00 p.m., with coverage available live on ESPN+.
